summary: The core is laid out as a netlist of the GX400 board. It has one module per Konami custom chip (K005289/5290/5291/5292/5293/5294/5295), an address decoder made of the board's 74138-style decoders named after their PCB locations, and DTACK and interrupt logic built from flip-flops clocked by CLK6, 1H/2H, VBLANK and 256V. Video is a per-pixel pipeline: raster counter bits drive scroll-RAM and VRAM fetches, shift registers, latch chains and a priority-mode combiner, and sprites go through a DMA'd object table and a DRAM-style double frame buffer. None of this follows MAME's tilemap and draw_sprites batch structure. Only the input-adaptation wheel module and the memory map overlap with MAME, and both are neutral.

findings.note: The video is split into the board's Konami customs: K005292 for timing, K005291 for scroll/VRAM addressing, K005290 for tile shifters, K005293 for the color/priority mux, and K005295/K005294 for the sprite engine and sprite pixels. Ports carry chip-level signals such as ORINC, WRTIME2, CHAOV, OCA and COLORLATCH_n. MAME has no counterpart to this split, only one screen_update and one draw_sprites.

findings.signal: address decode as discrete decoder chips
findings.note: Chip selects are cascaded 3-to-8 decoders named by board location (u14j_en, u6j_g2b_n, u13g_g2a_n, u11e_sel_n), gated with AS/LDS/UDS. They produce board nets (CHARA, VZURE, VRAMCS1/2, OBJRAM, DATA_n, AFE_n), not MAME's address-map handler entries. The resulting map is neutral, but the form is hardware.

DTACK for video RAM and character RAM comes from flip-flops u_17e_top/u_17e_bottom/u_18f, clocked by CLK6, 1H and a CLK6/1H/2H gate. This is the board's bus contention with the video side, which MAME does not model.

The IRQ levels come from flip-flops (u_17f_top/bottom) edge-triggered by VBLANK and 256V and set by the LS259 latch outputs u11k_out[0:1]. MAME instead uses a scanline timer callback that checks scanline 240/0 and the frame parity.

u11k_out and u13j_out are bit-addressable latches, written one bit at a time through cpu_addr[3:1], with a data bit from D0 or D8. Flip, interrupt-enable and sound-on outputs are taken from their bits, the way the board's 74LS259s are wired.

The scroll-RAM, object-RAM and object-table addresses are concatenations of H/V counter bits (w_4hd, w_2h, 128V..1V, 8H..2HD), multiplexed by VCLK. The K005292 H/V counters reset to 128/248, and VCLK is a flip-flop of H-counter bits. Fetches happen at scan time, not in a per-frame batch.

findings.signal: per-pixel latch pipeline for tile attributes
findings.note: Tile priority, flip and color go through a chain of latches clocked by 4HD/2HD/SHIFT_A1/A2/SHIFT_B, matching the tile shifters' delays. The final color-RAM address is picked per pixel at cen6. MAME draws tilemap categories line by line instead (the TILEMAP_DRAW_CATEGORY loop).

Two tile layers' priority bits select one of 26 layer-order modes. Each mode combines the A/B/OBJ transparency bits into the mux selects S0_n/S1_n, the way per-pixel combinational logic would. MAME uses priority-bitmap categories and prio_zoom_transpen masks instead.

findings.signal: sprite DMA table and frame buffer instead of priority loop
findings.note: During DMA, sprite bytes are copied into a table addressed by {obj_pri, 8H,4H,2HD}, so the hardware sorts by priority. K005295 latches attributes in LATCH_A..F and draws into two DRAM-style object buffers with RAS/CAS and clear/write phases. MAME instead loops over priority 255..0, scans every sprite and calls prio_zoom_transpen.

findings.signal: zoom as accumulator, not MAME formula
findings.note: Horizontal and vertical zoom work by adding the 10-bit zoom value into an accumulator, with carry-out advancing tile-line counters. MAME's division-based scale constant does not appear.

The 16-bit control word puts steering, brake and accel in the same fields as MAME's handler, which a correct core must share. The module itself adapts MiSTer analog/digital input (rate limiting, graded accel), which is FPGA engineering, not board logic.
Fractional clock enables from the system clock and jtframe dual-port BRAMs standing in for the board's SRAMs/DRAMs are resource choices and count for neither side.
